title: What belongs in a pressure vessel RFQ?
summary: A practical pressure vessel RFQ checklist covering process conditions, design basis, materials, inspection, certification and quotation scope.
body:
A clear request for quotation (RFQ) helps a manufacturer assess the engineering scope, identify missing information and prepare a useful budgetary offer. For a custom industrial pressure vessel, begin with the process duty and the design basis rather than dimensions alone.

1. Define the process and operating conditions

  • Service and medium: fluid composition, phase, concentration and any relevant corrosive, toxic, flammable or solids-handling characteristics.
  • Operating conditions: normal flow or batch duty, operating pressure and temperature, and start-up, shutdown or cleaning conditions where relevant.
  • Design conditions: design pressure and temperature, including vacuum or external-pressure cases when applicable. State whether pressure values are gauge or absolute.
  • Capacity and arrangement: working and total volume, vertical or horizontal orientation, available space, support type and any transport limits.

2. Identify materials and mechanical requirements

Specify the required material grade where known, corrosion allowance, lining or cladding requirements, and any impact-test or heat-treatment requirements. Provide nozzle sizes, ratings, orientations and connection standards, plus required internals, jackets, coils, agitators or access openings. If the material grade or wall thickness has not been confirmed, label it as a preliminary assumption rather than a final requirement.

3. Confirm codes, inspection and documentation

State the applicable design and manufacturing code, such as ASME Section VIII or EN 13445, where required by the project. Clarify inspection and test requirements, for example weld examination, pressure testing, material certificates, inspection records, nameplate requirements and any third-party or regional conformity assessment. The applicable scope depends on the project specification and destination market.

4. Define the commercial scope

  • Engineering, drawings and calculations required with the offer or after order placement.
  • Painting, insulation, accessories, instruments and spare parts, if applicable.
  • Inspection, documentation, export packing, delivery basis and destination.
  • Required delivery date, quantity and whether installation or commissioning is included.

Can a budgetary quotation be prepared with missing data?

Often, yes. A preliminary quotation can be based on clearly stated assumptions, but unconfirmed design pressure, temperature, medium, materials or code requirements may change the design and price. The final design should be confirmed against the approved project specification before fabrication.

For a preliminary review, send the available datasheet, drawing or RFQ and mark any open points. Contact Tongyang Process to discuss the equipment scope and quotation basis.
